newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma approves 97 budget in second reading.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma approves 97 budget in second reading.

text.p: The State Duma lower house of the Russian parliament approved the second reading of the draft 1997 budget on Friday by 248 votes to 114.

The vote, brought forward from December 25, brings Russia closer to meeting its goal of having a 1997 budget in place by the end of 1996. The budget faces a third reading and needs backing from the Federation Council upper house and it must then be signed into law by President Boris Yeltsin.
The Duma, dominated by communists and nationalists, left the broad parameters of the budget unchanged from the first reading, approved on Sunday.
The draft envisages a deficit of 3.5 percent of gross domestic product on revenues of 434.4 trillion roubles and expenditures of 529.8 trillion roubles.
In the second reading, deputies made some adjustments to spending in certain areas.
Communist Party leaders had earlier this month called for the budget to be rejected when it was first debated but said they had decided to back the spending plans for the sake of national unity.

But Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin has promised to pay most budget debts and to create a investment fund which the government estimates will attract over 200 trillion roubles, conditions the communists said they required for supporting the plan.
Passage of the budget is seen as a pre-requisite for securing continued disbursal of a $10 billion International Monetary Fund loan to Russia in 1997.
